name: Data Structures
description: This course provides a fundamental understanding of data structures and algorithms, covering topics such as arrays, linked lists, trees, graphs, sorting and searching algorithms, and complexity analysis. Students will develop problem-solving skills and implement algorithms in a programming language of choice, focusing on efficiency and scalability.

name: World Geography
description: This course explores the physical and human geography of the world, examining landforms, climate, ecosystems, population distribution, and cultural landscapes. Students will analyze geographic trends, global issues, and the impact of human activities on the environment through case studies and interactive mapping exercises.

name: Linear Algebra
description: This course introduces students to the fundamental concepts of linear algebra, including vector spaces, matrices, determinants, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and linear transformations. Applications in physics, computer science, and engineering are explored, along with computational methods for solving linear systems.

name: Classical Mechanics
description: This course covers the principles of classical mechanics, including Newtonian mechanics, kinematics, dynamics, work and energy, momentum, rotational motion, and harmonic motion. Students will develop problem-solving skills through mathematical modeling and real-world physics applications.

name: Introduction to Literature
description: This course provides an introduction to literary analysis through the study of poetry, fiction, and drama. Students will explore literary themes, narrative techniques, and historical contexts while developing critical thinking and analytical writing skills. Readings include works from diverse authors and literary traditions.

name: World History: Ancient to Modern
description: This course examines major historical events and civilizations from ancient times to the modern era, focusing on cultural, political, and economic developments. Topics include ancient empires, medieval societies, revolutions, and globalization. Students will analyze historical sources and explore connections between past and present.
